# Bhaddiya Sutta (Ud 2.10 (PTS Ud 18))
**ID:** Ud 2.10 (PTS Ud 18)
**Section:** Udāna (ud)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Bhaddiya Sutta* (Ud 2.10; PTS Ud 18) is the tenth discourse of the second chapter of the *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts an inspired exclamation by the monk Bhaddiya (the son of Lady Kāḷigodhā), a former Sakyan royal who had gone forth into the monastic order alongside Anuruddha and other nobles [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Horner, Cullavagga]. While dwelling in solitude beneath a tree in the forest, Bhaddiya repeatedly exclaims over the bliss of his state [SuttaCentral; Buswell & Lopez 2014; Horner, Cullavagga]. Overhearing his cries, other monks suspect that he is reminiscing about the lost luxuries and status of his former rulership and report him to the Buddha [Horner, Cullavagga]. When questioned, Bhaddiya clarifies that while he formerly lived in constant dread, suspicion, and anxiety despite being surrounded by heavily armed guards, he now dwells peaceful, fearless, and unburdened in the forest, prompting the Buddha to utter an inspired utterance (*udāna*) celebrating his release [SuttaCentral; Horner, Cullavagga].
SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree that this discourse is closely paralleled by the account of Bhaddiya's renunciation and awakening found in the *Saṁghabhedakakkhandhaka* of the Vinaya Piṭaka (Kd 17) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies 46 matching passages between Ud 2.10 and Kd 17 totaling 7,703 shared characters, with a continuous alignment between §2.5–9.4 of the sutta and §1.5.1–2.1.0 of Kd 17 at a similarity of 0.9 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, SuttaCentral records a passage-level parallel to the *Uraga Sutta* (Snp 1.1), as well as verse parallels in the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* (*Sukhavarga*, UV 30, UVS 30, and Uv Kg 30) and Chinese translation collections (T 212.31 and T 213.30) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus also records widespread internal Pali formulaic reuse, most prominently with the Dasakanipāta (AN 10, 50 matches), the Pañcakanipāta (AN 5, 33 matches), and the Bhikkhu Saṁyutta (SN 21, 14 matches) [DharmaNexus].
